name: Delilah
bio:
Delilah was a woman from the valley of Sorek, the one Samson loved, who was bribed by Philistine leaders to repeatedly probe the secret of his strength and ultimately betrayed him — making her one of Scripture's most well-known examples of betrayal.

Philistine leaders approached Delilah, promising her eleven hundred shekels of silver each if she could discover the source of Samson's strength so they could subdue him (Judges 16:5). Delilah pressed Samson three times, and each time he lied — first about undried vine ropes, then new ropes, then weaving his hair into a loom — and each time Philistines lay in ambush in the room, yet his true strength remained undiscovered (Judges 16:6-14).

After three failed attempts, Delilah nagged him daily until he was tired to death, and Samson finally told her the truth: his strength lay entirely in his hair, which had never been cut because he was a Nazirite (Judges 16:15-17). Delilah had his hair shaved off while he slept and, once his strength was gone, handed him over to the Philistines, who immediately gouged out his eyes and imprisoned him for hard labor (Judges 16:18-21).

Because of this betrayal, Delilah's name has become, in Scripture and in later culture alike, the enduring symbol of betraying someone you love for personal gain.
